summary: Taitsu Kono is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Hanazono University (~1950–1954) and under traditional teacher Mumon Yamada (~1954–1988), later holding a post at Hanazono University (~1993–1997).

Taixu was a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher. He studied under Jing'an, Jichan, and Renshan Yang, including at Jinling Scriptural Press. He served at Bilu Temple and led the Minnan Buddhist Institute, which he founded in 1918.

Taizan Maezumi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, San Francisco State University, and under Hakujun Kuroda, Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, and Koryu Osaka. He served as a priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission in 1956.
Tak Pui Sze is a scholar in sinology and religious studies who completed PhD studies at the University of British Columbia under doctoral supervisor Jinhua Chen (attested 2012).

Taka Yanagisawa was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Japan Women's University. She served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.
Takahiko Kameyama works in Buddhist studies. In 2015, he was attested as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.
Takahiko Sato is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested in 2015 and 2026).

Takahiro Asano works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Chiba, Doshisha, Washington, and York universities. He held posts at Kyoto International Social Welfare Exchange Centre, Japan Lutheran College (2021–2026), and Musashino University (2026).
Takahiro Kato is an Indology and philosophy scholar. As of 2026, he is attested as a professor at the University of Tokyo and affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Takako Abe works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She has held posts at Taisho University, serving as a lecturer (attested 2013–2017) and faculty member (attested 2026).

Takamaro Shigaraki was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University and studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and Institute of Buddhist Studies. He was a professor and president (1989–1995) at Ryukoku University.

Takamatsu Yoshie studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō, Waseda University, and the University of Paris. He held teaching posts at Waseda Junior and Senior High School and Waseda University, where he served as Dean of the School of Humanities.

Takami Inoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Inoue was a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takamichi Fukita is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho and Bukkyo universities under Zenno Ishigami, Heinz Bechert, Shozen Kumoi, and Yuichi Kajiyama, later lecturing at Bukkyo University (attested 1999, 2013).

Takanobu Takahashi is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Tamilannal, and Utrecht University (PhD). He held posts at Shitennoji University and the University of Tokyo (1996; 1999–2016).
Takanori Fukita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a graduate student at Bukkyo University (attested 2017) and held a teaching post as lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Takanori Shintani is a scholar in religious studies and Japanology who studied at Waseda University. He has held academic posts at Kokugakuin University and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.

Takanori Unno was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Nagoya University, studying under numerous scholars including Yoshifumi Ueda. He held posts at Nagoya University, Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music, and Meijo University.

Takao Hayashi is an Indology and history scholar who earned degrees from Tohoku, Kyoto, and Brown universities under David Pingree and others. He held posts at Harish-Chandra Research Institute, Kyoto Women's University, and Doshisha University (1986–1989; 1995–2015).
Takao Kagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba, and served as a professor at Bukkyo University.
